package_info.package_versions: maliciously tampered version released in late March 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp package was maliciously tampered with during its build process, resulting in the distribution of software containing embedded malicious code to end users. This code was not present in the original source and was introduced as part of a targeted supply chain attack, enabling threat actors to compromise the systems of 3CX customers.

execution_context.file_location: 3CXDesktopApp build artifacts (exact file unspecified, but within the distributed application binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code was injected into the 3CXDesktopApp binary during the build process, enabling the application to execute unauthorized network communications and potentially download further payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely C++/JavaScript, depending on app tech stack)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, potentially downloading additional payloads or exfiltrating sensitive data from the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code was not present in the legitimate source and was introduced only in the build artifacts, indicating unauthorized tampering. Outbound network connections to unknown domains from a desktop application are highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application builds should not include code that initiates covert network communications or downloads further executables post-installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automatic update mechanisms may contact vendor servers, but should be well-documented and use trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Code present only in built artifacts, not in source
Outbound network connections to non-3CX domains
Potential for downloading and executing further payloads

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the 3CXDesktopApp during the build process via compromised CI/CD pipeline.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of tampered application to end users

attack_chain.action: End users install and run the tampered 3CXDesktopApp, which executes the embedded malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code initiates network connections to attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malicious code may download additional payloads or exfiltrate sensitive data from the victim's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full compromise of victim systems

behavioral_signatures: Presence of code in build artifacts not found in source repository
Unexpected outbound network connections from desktop application
Application downloading and executing additional payloads post-install
file_indicators: 3CXDesktopApp binaries with hash mismatches compared to official source
Unexplained changes in application binary size or structure
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs not associated with 3CX
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP(S) requests from the application
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for discrepancies between source code and build artifacts, especially unexpected code or resources in distributed binaries. Analyze network traffic from installed applications for connections to untrusted domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in application binaries. Employ behavioral analysis to flag applications that download and execute additional code post-installation.
